vedic_reference.note: Sushrut is a legendary surgeon mentioned in the Indian epic, Mahabharata. He is known for his great surgical skills and is considered the pioneer of Ayurvedic surgery.

data.cultural_impact: Sushrut is a prominent name in Indian history and culture, particularly in the realm of Ayurvedic medicine. Sushrut is the name of a legendary surgeon, consider the father of medicine in ancient India. He is the main author of the ancient Sanskrit text, "Sushruta-samhita," which is one of the foundational works of Ayurveda. The name Sushrut continues to be revered and respected for its association with surgical expertise and the tradition of Ayurvedic medicine.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Sushrut carries spiritual significance as it honors the divine power of healing. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words "su" meaning good or excellent, and "shrut," meaning ear or hearing. This signifies that one who hears orlistens to the wisdom of the scriptures and applies them healing ailments, both physical and spiritual, is truly blessed. So, the name Sushrut is a constant reminder of the importance of seeking and sharing knowledge and the power of the Divine in the healing process.

historical_references.reference: Sushrut is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata, as a skilled surgeon and the author of the Sushruta Samhita, a seminal text on Ayurvedic medicine.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sushrut remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Maya Sushrut in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Sushrut, which means "Healer". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Sushrut symbolizes profound wisdom and precision in healing. As a renowned ancient Indian surgeon, he embodies the healing power of knowledge and skillful hands.
